title: Nādānusandhāna

attribution.tradition: Spoken by Śiva to the Goddess.

structure.description: a short tract of a few dozen verses (not counted precisely)

summary: A short dialogue in which Śiva teaches the unstruck inner sound in ten forms (ciṇī, ciñciṇī, ciri, conch, strings, a ringing, bronze cymbals, cloud, roaring water, kettle-drum) — the first nine to be left and the tenth giving liberation — and correlates the sounds with the elements and their maṇḍalas and with the dissolution of the principles.
notes: Distinct from the Nādabindu Upaniṣad and from the nāda chapter of the Haṭhapradīpikā. Date and provenance unknown to this unit. The e-texts are corrupt in places.
